top.title: Couch: 3 quick takes on Michigan State basketball's 106-72 win over Northern Iowa
top.description: 1. 106 points scored, but some lesson for MSU against Northern Iowa EAST LANSING — With the score 19-2, barely more than five minutes into the game, you had to wonder if Northern Iowa could get to 10. Michigan State’s defense was that relentless. The Panthers looked that overwhelmed. By halftime, Northern Iowa had 44 points. MSU 59. The officials 33 fouls called, playing their part in what might have been a very watchable half, but instead wasn’t. Two minutes into the second half, it was MSU 62, Northern Iowa 51. This as an actual game, with Jasah Jervis’ 3-point shooting primarily responsible for keeping the Panthers at bay. In the end, it was a comfortable 106-72 MSU win over an offensively skilled opponent that had a lot more faith in its ability to shoot and score than it appeared in the opening minutes. There are couple lessons MSU can take from this game: One, that you can’t knock out every lesser foe with an early punch. Some of these teams have some confident dudes who play. If you see a team with two or three guys on the court who look like Howdy Doody, assume they can shoot and are better than they look. They’re out there for a reason. Second, MSU has to learn how to be physical defensively and on the glass without fouling. Because while the Spartans withstood having seven players with two fouls each in the first half Friday, that’ll be a problem against some opponents. The officials were too quick with the whistle Friday. There were a number of fouls called that just weren’t. But there were a lot that were. This was a handsy and physical game, a clumsily physical game in the first half especially. Ultimately, we’re nitpicking a 34-point win over a solid Missouri Valley Conference team where the Spartans scored over 100 points, got 44 points out of their starting backcourt (Jeremy Fears Jr., 24, and Jervis, 20) and took control firmly as the second half went along. But that’s where this team is now. After Tuesday’s wire to wire win over Duke, all that’s left to do against Northern Iowa is nitpick. And this group left Tom Izzo plenty to pick at. 2. Jervis, again, leads record 3-point shooting night It’s becoming clear shooting isn’t going to be a problem for this MSU basketball team. And that it’ll likely be a strength. You can’t take that just from a record-setting night against Northern Iowa, where the Spartans hit a program-record 18 3-pointers (on 37 attempts) against a Northern Iowa team that’s never heard of a close-out defensively. Still, no team has ever hit that many before and MSU has played a zillion poor defensive teams since the 3-point shot came into play in the 1980s. Jeremy Fears hit 4 of 5 3-point attempts, Jordan Scott 3 of 5, Jesse McCulloch 2 of 2, and freshman Jasiah Jervis 5 of 6, on his way to 20 points. He’s hit 12 of 23 3s through four games this season. The Cleveland Guardians need offensive help. While the Guardians are going to pursue pitching depth as well, signing one or two hitters wouldn’t be a bad idea. There is one specific free agent who makes perfect sense for Cleveland. While the Guards are not expected to spend much money in MLB free agency once again, Ty France represents an ideal fit. He had a big season but won’t command as much money as other stars in free agency, and he’d address the Guardians’ first base uncertainty. France somewhat quietly enjoyed a big 2026 season with the San Diego Padres. The right-handed slugger hit .295/.363/.502 to go along with an .865 OPS, 21 home runs and 24 doubles. France, a former All-Star and Gold Glove winner, is capable of playing first, second or third base, but he spent most of his time at first in 2026. Cleveland began the ’26 campaign with a platoon of Rhys Hoskins and Kyle Manzardo at first base. Manzardo was ultimately sent down to Triple-A due to underperformance while Hoskins landed on the injured list. The Guards acquired Nathaniel Lowe at the MLB trade deadline. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) France wouldn’t require a platoon, though. He recorded an .869 OPS against right-handers and an .853 OPS against left-handers this past season. It is worth mentioning that one of Cleveland’s top prospects, Ralphy Velazquez, is a first baseman who is almost ready for the big leagues. With that being said, there are no guarantees he will begin the ’27 season with the MLB ball club. Additionally, Velasquez is versatile, as he’s spent time at catcher and in the outfield in addition to first base at the minor league level. As mentioned, one of the Guardians priorities is to add pitching depth this offseason. Upgrading the offense also needs to be a goal, though. The Guardians should at least consider pursuing Ty France in free agency. top.title: John Fisher to sell San Jose Earthquakes, PayPal Park for $625M
top.description: A San Jose Earthquakes flag is seen during a MLS match between the San Jose Earthquakes and Houston Dynamo FC on Sept. 12, 2026 at PayPal Park in San Jose. (Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Less than two weeks before the San Jose Earthquakes are scheduled to finally play their very first playoff match at PayPal Park, owner John Fisher is selling the team. On Friday, the Earthquakes announced that Heath Freeman, a media executive best known for being the co-founder and president of hedge fund Alden Global Capital, has agreed to purchase the team and its home stadium from Fisher and his partners. Major League Soccer's board has already approved the ownership change, the team said, and "the transaction is expected to close in the coming weeks." Sportico was first to report about Fisher's sale to Freeman and reported the sale price was $625 million, a figure that an Earthquakes team official confirmed was accurate to SFGATE. Fisher has been looking to sell the Earthquakes since June 2025. At the time, Fisher was in the beginning stages of building the A's ballpark in Las Vegas, and was seeking more finances to build the new stadium. The Las Vegas ballpark 's construction has progressed steadily, but the estimated cost has ballooned from as low as $1.5 billion originally to north of $2 billion . The reviled A's owner purchased the Quakes in 2007, getting a chance to revive the MLS franchise after the first iteration of the club ended when the franchise moved to Houston. Fisher privately financed the building of the stadium now known as PayPal Park, spending $100 million to build the stadium that opened in 2015. Between the A's move to Las Vegas and the pending Earthquakes sale, it seems Fisher will now no longer be a sports owner in the region that his family has called home for his entire life. Freeman is a graduate of Duke who played on the school's football team as a walk-on kicker. An avid sports fan, he's an owner of a Professional Bull Riders team, the executive chairman of the AVP beach volleyball league, and a major booster of his alma mater as well as the University of Miami's volleyball team. Outside of the sports world, Freeman has become a vilified figure in the media world thanks to the moves of Alden. The hedge fund has become notorious for buying newspapers, slashing jobs and leaving skeleton crews to continue working while Alden takes home massive profits . This has even played out in the Bay Area, as one of Alden's newspaper companies, Digital First Media, has turned a number of regional newspapers - the San Jose Mercury News, the Oakland Tribune, the Contra Costa Times and more - into a single company, the Bay Area News Group. "Our vision is simple – winning on and off the field for San Jose and the entire region," Freeman said in a statement provided by the Earthquakes. top.description: The 49ers are supposed to fly to Dallas this weekend for a game against the Cowboys. In this file photo, members of the 49ers organization depart on a chartered flight from Mineta San Jose International Airport on Jan. 26, 2020. (Jim Gensheimer/Special to The Chronicle) San Jose State's football team reached the travel equivalent of the 1-yard line, but the Spartans couldn't quite get into the end zone. SJSU's charter flight Friday, bound for Colorado Springs and Saturday's game against Air Force, made it to the runway at San Jose's airport. Then the Federal Aviation Administration's ground stop order abruptly halted air traffic nationwide. So the plane, with a traveling party of more than 100 football players, coaches and school officials, stopped and waited - and eventually returned to the gate. The Spartans later headed back to their football facility on campus, and now they hope to make the trip early Saturday morning. Kickoff is scheduled for 4 p.m PST (5 p.m. MST) in Colorado. "We were on the taxiway, No. 2 for takeoff on one side, and the pilot came on and said they were having computer issues," said Sky Kerstein, SJSU's associate athletics director for communications and broadcasting. "He said it would be a quick deal. I'm a big aviation nerd, so I checked on my phone and realized it was a lot more than that. "Then the pilot turned off the engines. I listened to air traffic control and heard other pilots saying they wanted to go back to the gate. When that happens, you know it's going to be a long delay." San Jose State's traveling party hung out on the plane for about two hours, Kerstein said, before re-boarding four buses for the short drive back to campus. The group originally was hoping to resume its trip Friday night, a plan now pushed back to Saturday morning. The FAA lifted its ground stop about 5:30 on Friday evening. • Cal and Stanford are both playing on the road Saturday, but the Bears and Cardinal traveled Thursday because of their long, cross-country journeys. Cal plays at Virginia and Stanford faces Virginia Tech. San Jose State players and coaches showed little frustration with their aborted trip, according to Kerstein. They held their customary Friday night meetings - which usually happen at the team hotel - Friday afternoon at the football facility on campus in San Jose. "People were upbeat on the plane," Kerstein said. "I had CNN on my iPad, so they were asking me what was going on. We're fed very well on these flights, and food makes everybody happy." • Cal's women's basketball team was scheduled to travel to Santa Barbara by plane Friday, ahead of Saturday's noon game against UCSB. top.title: Jeremy Fears Jr. Jasiah Jervis jump all over Northern Iowa
top.description: EAST LANSING – Tom Izzo wanted to see how Michigan State basketball would respond to success. The Spartans did so in triplicate. Jeremy Fears Jr. and Jasiah Jervis led an outside shooting barrage for No. 5 MSU, which broke a school record with 18 3-pointers en route to a 104-72 victory over Northern Iowa on Friday, Nov. 13, at Breslin Center. ON GUARD: Michigan State's ferocious defense is its 'best brand of basketball' The previous single-game record was 17 3-pointers, set against Purdue on Feb. 20, 2014, and tied against Rutgers on Jan. 31, 2016. Fears finished with 24 points and nine assists, while Jervis scored 20 points as the two combined for nine of the 3s for the Spartans (4-0). Jordan Scott had 11 first-half points and made three more 3s, while Jesse McCulloch and Kur Teng each hit a pair from deep. Freshman Julius Avent drained the record-breaker with 50 seconds to play as MSU finished 18-for-37 (48.6%) from behind the arc. The Spartans also turned 16 UNI turnovers into 31 points. Greyson Uelmen scored 16 points and three others added 11 apiece for the Panthers (2-2). It was over when ... MSU put the game away swiftly, with a 19-2 opening salvo that included five 3-pointers in six attempts. Fears and Scott had two apiece, and Jervis had another. The Spartans built their lead to 20 on Jervis’ second 3 as part of a 7-for-9 start beyond the arc. By halftime, five different MSU players hit at least one 3-pointer. Scott had three 3s and 11 points with four boards at the break. That sizzling 10-for-16 shot-making from deep led to a 59-44 halftime advantage, the most points the Spartans have scored in a first half since getting 64 in a 104-83 blowout of Green Bay on Dec. 18, 2018. Then after UNI trimmed MSU’s cushion to 11 points less than 2 minutes into the second half, the Spartans’ 3-point shooting again put them over the edge with two from Jervis and one from Fears. McCulloch and Teng followed with two more to rebuild the lead to 71-56, and then the Spartans ripped off a 21-0 burst over a six-minute stretch to remove any doubt. Player of the game: Jeremy Fears Jr. Fears carried over his stellar showing from Tuesday night’s 79-73 victory over No. 2 Duke in the Champions Classic by coming out firing early. Fears had 19 points by halftime and was 5-for-5 from the field (and 3-for-3 from 3-point range) with four assists. After setting up Jervis for another 3 to open the second-half scoring, Fears followed his first miss from deep with his fourth 3-pointer to give MSU a 68-54 lead less than four minutes into the final period. The reigning All-American finished 6-for-7 shooting and 4-of-5 from deep in 28 minutes. Fears had 18 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds Tuesday against the Blue Devils. Trending up: Jasiah Jervis Jervis continues to show few nerves as a freshman in the starting lineup. top.title: UNC handed first loss of the season in sloppy game against Georgia
top.description: Nov 13, 2026; Chapel Hill, North Carolina, USA; Georgia Bulldogs guard Marcus Millender (4) lays the ball up against North Carolina Tar Heels guard Neo Avdalas (17) and guard Terrence Brown (1) during the first half at Smith Center. Mandatory Credit: Zachary Taft-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Unlike UNC’s game against Wyoming on Tuesday, the Tar Heels turned in a first half they couldn’t fully make up for in their 78-70 loss to Georgia on Friday. Carolina shot just 25% from the field and from three in the first 20 minutes and allowed the Bulldogs to close on a 9-0 run to hold a 38-31 advantage at the break. The loss snapped a 21-game win streak at the Dean Dome for the Heels. The second half was definitely a better offensive effort for UNC. They shot 40% from the field in the second half. Georgia was able to make 14 three-pointers, though, and that was enough to come out on top of a close game. Terrence Brown was very good again, leading the team with 21 points and zero turnovers. Neo Avdalas and Isaiah Denis were the only other Tar Heels in double figures with 14 and 11 points, respectively. Carolina made just nine of their 38 three-point attempts. They were also pushed around on the boards again, losing the battle on the glass 52-43. Carolina led by as many as nine points in the game, and looked in the second half like they may have figured things out similarly to their win earlier in the week. Georgia is not Wyoming, though, and they were not going to go down easily. The Heels’ poor rebounding and lack of offensive efficiency, combined with the Bulldogs’ threes, proved to be enough for Georgia to walk away with a win. It was an immensely frustrating game because it was very easy to see how the outcome could have been different. Allowing Georgia extra possessions often ended with the Bulldogs getting another three. Carolina also seemingly abandoned running actual offense down the stretch to their detriment as the game slipped away. These are not things you can afford to do against real Power 4 competition. UNC will have a week to fix what they can ahead of next Friday’s game against Marshall.

top.title: Record pace from 3 powers Michigan State to 106-72 win over UNI
top.description: EAST LANSING — Jordan Scott drilled a 3 from the corner to open the game and from that point on, Michigan State was never particularly threatened in what turned into a blowout win. The Spartans poured in early 3s from Scott, Jasiah Jervis and Jeremy Fears Jr., smothered Northern Iowa to four points in the opening 5:34, and built an early double-digit lead that held the rest of the way as Michigan State (4-0) shot its way to a 106-72 win over Northern Iowa on Friday, Nov. 13 at the Breslin Center. MSU made 3s at record pace on Friday night against UNI (2-2), making 18 to set the new program record, surpassing the previous mark of 17. MSU had made 17 3s in a game twice previously: vs. Rutgers in 2016 and vs. Purdue in 2014. More: MSU's Jordan Scott shows fruits of offseason defensive work vs. Duke Fears, Scott, Jervis, Kur Teng and Jesse McCulloch each made multiple 3s. Fears Jr. finished with 24 points and nine assists, and went 4-of-5 from beyond the arc, with just the lone miss all game. Jervis added 20 points and five made 3s. Scott, who in the second half was seen on the bench with ice on his right shoulder, scored 11 points, as did Coen Carr. It also turned into a foul filled affair, with 61 total fouls, leading to a combined 69 free throws for both teams. MSU went 32-of-43 from the line. Michigan State pulled away with a barrage of early 3s, opening the game with three-straight makes from behind the arc, first by Jordan Scott in the right corner, then Jasiah Jervis from the same spot. Jeremy Fears Jr. added a third 3 from closer to the top of the arc. When MSU did finally miss a 3, on the fourth try of the game, Cam Ward came down with the rebound from Scott’s long miss, possession recycled, and Fears stepped into another three from about the same spot that he made the first from. Fears himself was a perfect 5-of-5 from the field in the first half, including a trio of triples. top.title: Joshua Kimmich proud of Germany’s ‘thoroughly deserved win’ against Serbia
top.description: Photo by UEFA Photo/UEFA via Getty Images | UEFA via Getty Images Germany produced a strong first-half showing against Serbia. Jürgen Klopp’s men applied pressure early, forcing an own goal from left-back Srđan Babić after just three minutes of play. Florian Wirtz doubled Germany’s lead 11 minutes later. Klopp’s side finished the first half two goals to the good. Germany picked up where they left off at the start of the second half, with Brajan Gruda scoring his first-ever goal for the national team in the 50th minute. However, Serbia would strike back. Just six minutes later, Babić made up for his first-half mistake by scoring — on the correct side of the field this time. Germany walked away with a largely dominant 3-1 victory . But don’t let the scoreline fool you. After Serbia’s goal, the match became chaotic, and according to Germany captain Joshua Kimmich, the hosts created a few problems for his side. “I thought the first half was very good,” said Kimmich (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). “I think we played some good football. We had a few problems after the break, and things became a little hectic. Serbia played a lot of long balls, and the pitch also became difficult to play on towards the end. (AP) — Alex Wilkins made a 3-pointer with 2.1 seconds remaining to lift No. 24 Kentucky to a 78-77 win over Northern Arizona on Friday night. Coming off a 89-69 loss to No. 15 Kansas in the Champions Classic on Tuesday night, Kentucky overcame 13 lead changes and four ties to hold off the Lumberjacks. Wilkins rescued the Wildcats (3-1), who trailed by four points, at 77-73, with 18 seconds remaining. The Lumberjacks (0-4) missed two free throws in the final 13 seconds as Kentucky survived the upset bid. Milan Momcilovic and Malachi Moreno added 14 points each for the Wildcats. Ousman N’Diaye scored 11 and Justin McBride 10. Kentucky trailed by five in the second half after leading by 13 in the first half. nigeria.title: Emefiele: Court admits Supreme Court judgment in forfeiture case
nigeria.description: —Restricts use of document in ongoing criminal trial By Henry Ojelu The Lagos State Special Offences Court, Ikeja, on Friday admitted a Supreme Court judgment tendered by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, in the ongoing trial of former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Godwin Emefiele, over the forfeiture of properties allegedly linked to him. However, the trial judge, Justice Rahman Oshodi, ruled that although the judgment was admissible, it could not be used for or against any of the parties in the criminal proceedings. Ruling on objections raised by the defence, led by Olalekan Ojo, SAN, and submissions by the prosecution, led by the Federal Director of Public Prosecutions, Rotimi Oyedepo, SAN, Justice Oshodi held that the document was a public document and a certified true copy of a Supreme Court decision. The judge consequently admitted it as Exhibit A but restricted its use in the trial. He said: “The judgment is a public document, and it is a certified true copy of the Supreme Court decision. It would be accepted as an exhibit (in rem), but cannot be used in the case either for or against any party.” Justice Oshodi explained that the document satisfied the legal requirements for admissibility under the Evidence Act. On the defence’s objection that the prosecution tendered only the lead judgment without the separate judgments of other Supreme Court justices, the judge relied on the Court of Appeal decision in Matthias Sikiri and Others v. Nketchukwu Onyema and Others (2021) LPELR-56552(CA). He also cited Avacha and Others v. Fawole, where the Supreme Court held that the lead judgment represents the decision of the court. Addressing concerns over the use of a judgment arising from civil forfeiture proceedings in a criminal trial, Justice Oshodi said the restriction on its use had adequately addressed the issue. Citing David Itauma v. Friday Jasi, the judge said previous judgments tendered in subsequent proceedings were intended to establish what was decided in the earlier cases and not to prove the guilt or innocence of parties in the subsequent proceedings. He consequently overruled the defence objection and admitted the document. Earlier, Ojo had opposed its admission, arguing that the judgment was irrelevant to the charges against his client, incomplete without the other justices’ opinions and arose from non-conviction-based civil forfeiture proceedings. Counsel to the second defendant, A.M. Kotoye, SAN, aligned himself with the objection and urged the court to reject the document. However, Oyedepo argued that the judgment was admissible as a certified true copy of a Supreme Court decision, adding that the prosecution had complied with Sections 103 and 104 of the Evidence Act. He maintained that the fact that only the lead judgment was tendered did not affect its admissibility, while the civil nature of the forfeiture proceedings did not make the document inadmissible. nigeria.title: FG records 16 Nigerian deaths in Addis Ababa, warns travellers
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has warned Nigerians, particularly those with pre-existing medical conditions, to exercise caution when travelling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, following the deaths of 16 Nigerians in the city this year. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a travel advisory issued on Friday, stating that the deaths recorded by Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa were reportedly linked to health complications associated with the city’s high altitude. The ministry explained that Addis Ababa is situated approximately 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure results in reduced oxygen availability. It noted that the conditions could pose increased health risks to travellers with certain underlying medical conditions, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory ailments. According to the advisory, although healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, people with certain pre-existing health conditions may experience complications. The Federal Government therefore advised Nigerians whose medical conditions could be worsened by high altitudes to seek appropriate medical advice before undertaking journeys involving transit through the Ethiopian capital. It also urged travellers with underlying medical conditions to consult medical professionals and obtain necessary guidance before embarking on their trips. The ministry, however, clarified that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa. Rather, it said the notice was aimed at ensuring that medically vulnerable travellers were adequately informed about the possible effects of high altitudes and took necessary precautions. nigeria.title: Goalkeeper Owono suspended for 12 matches after De Miguel death
nigeria.description: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono was suspended for 12 matches by the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee on Friday after his challenge on Jesus de Miguel resulted in the death of the Tenerife striker last week. Equatorial Guinea international Owono was sent off in the second division clash on November 2 after racing into midfield and colliding with De Miguel while trying to clear an aerial ball. After the collision De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and the Spanish forward died on November 3. “The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’,” said the committee in a statement. “The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge. “In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.” Spanish police sources last week told AFP an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision. Owono said he was enduring the “hardest days of my life” after De Miguel’s death. “These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra last week. “I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him. “I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus.” FC Andorra coach Carles Manso said Thursday it would be Owono who decides if and when he returns to football after the tragic incident. On Saturday Tenerife fans and players gathered at the club’s stadium for a memorial and farewell to De Miguel. His funeral took place last Thursday and around 400 mourners attended, including Spain coach Luis de la Fuente and Real Madrid president Florentino Perez. Adeoye said the disruption of the meeting at Classique Event Centre, Oregun, Ikeja, on Thursday, amounted to an infringement on the constitutional rights of citizens to assemble and freely express their political views. nigeria.title: Nasarawa pensioners begin enforcement of ₦4bn court order
nigeria.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia A group of 601 retired civil servants in Nasarawa State has commenced enforcement of a court order directing the recovery of over ₦4 billion in outstanding gratuities and other entitlements owed them by the state government. The pensioners, under the aegis of the Concerned Group of Nasarawa State Pensioners, secured a consent judgment against the state government in 2020 over the alleged non-payment of their retirement benefits. Their spokespersons, Mr Simon Auna and Mallam Usman Adamu, disclosed the development while speaking with journalists in Lafia on Friday. The group said it subsequently obtained an order from the National Industrial Court, Makurdi, awarding 25 per cent post-judgment interest on the judgment sum, bringing the total amount being sought to over ₦4 billion. According to the pensioners, following the alleged failure of the state government to comply with the judgment, their lawyers approached the Senior District Court in Makurdi, presided over by Justice Ada Jack. The court subsequently directed six commercial banks to release funds belonging to the Nasarawa State Government, amounting to over ₦4 billion, for payment to the affected retirees. In a move to enforce the order, the pensioners’ legal team, accompanied by court bailiffs, visited some branches of one of the commercial banks in Makurdi, Benue State, where they removed some movable properties. Speaking on the development, counsel to the pensioners, Mrs Doofan Sefa-Aii, said the legal team would continue to operate within the law to ensure full recovery of the funds owed the retirees. Another counsel, Mr Awo Matthew, appealed to the Nasarawa State Government and the banks involved to allow the legal process to take its course, considering the hardship the pensioners had endured while pursuing payment of their entitlements. However, the Director of Corporate Services and Arbitration at the Nasarawa State Ministry of Justice, Mr Usman Aliyu, said the state government had taken all necessary legal steps, including filing a motion for a stay of execution of the court order. Meanwhile, Adamu, who is the group’s Lafia Local Government Chairman, and Auna, its Legal Adviser, described the court order as a significant breakthrough after years of seeking payment of their entitlements. They said the development had renewed their hope of recovering the outstanding benefits. The pensioners reaffirmed their determination to pursue their entitlements through lawful means until the matter was resolved. Zulum gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the headquarters of the 24 Task Force Brigade in Dikwa Local Government Area, where he met with the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General Aminu Gumel. The governor said the visit was aimed at exploring measures to improve security along the Maiduguri–Mafa–Dikwa–Ngala highway, a strategic economic corridor linking several communities in eastern Borno State. He noted that the highway was vital to trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities, stressing that improved security would enable residents to travel safely, move agricultural produce and rebuild their livelihoods. “My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said. Addressing troops preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe, the governor pledged to provide operational logistics and sustained welfare support. He also announced a payment of ₦50,000 to each soldier preparing for the deployment to the two communities. Koshebe has previously suffered deadly attacks by suspected Boko Haram insurgents. On November 28, 2020, insurgents attacked rice farmers working in fields around the community, killing more than 100 people, many of whom were seasonal farm labourers from Sokoto State. nigeria.title: COVID-19 loans must be repaid, NIRSAL MFB insists
nigeria.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief NIRSAL Microfinance Bank (NMFB) has clarified that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility (TCF) was an intervention loan, not a grant, stressing that beneficiaries are obligated to repay the funds. The bank said deductions from the accounts of beneficiaries who accessed the facility would continue until their outstanding loans were fully liquidated, in line with the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism. In a statement issued in Abuja at the weekend, the bank explained that the GSI framework allows financial institutions to recover outstanding loan obligations from eligible accounts linked to borrowers’ Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs), subject to applicable regulatory guidelines. The bank said the clarification became necessary to address concerns surrounding loan recoveries and reassure customers and members of the public of its commitment to transparency, accountability and responsible banking practices. It explained that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility was introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to support households and businesses affected by the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. According to the bank, all beneficiaries were required to accept electronic offer letters before disbursement, with the documents clearly outlining the terms and conditions of the facility, including repayment obligations and recovery mechanisms in cases of default. “Regarding the recovery process, the Bank operates within the applicable regulatory framework, including the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism approved by the Central Bank of Nigeria,” it stated. NIRSAL MFB, however, acknowledged concerns raised by some beneficiaries over the timing and amounts of deductions, outstanding loan balances and access to repayment information. The bank said it took the complaints seriously, noting that customers must have access to accurate information about their loan accounts. It stressed that the deductions were intended to settle outstanding contractual obligations, adding that beneficiaries who disputed deductions or identified discrepancies in their repayment records should contact the bank for individual account reconciliation. “Where any beneficiary has concerns about deductions made, discrepancies in repayment records or the status of an outstanding balance, such cases should be brought to the bank’s attention for individual account reconciliation and appropriate resolution,” it said. The bank assured that legitimate complaints would be investigated and that any discrepancies established during the reconciliation process would receive the necessary attention. It urged beneficiaries seeking clarification on their loan status, repayment history or outstanding obligations to contact the bank through its officially designated customer service channels. nigeria.title: Customs intercepts live sea turtle at Nigeria-Benin border
nigeria.description: By Efe Onodjae The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Seme Area Command, has intercepted a live endangered sea turtle allegedly being smuggled through a footpath linking Nigeria and the Republic of Benin. The Olive Ridley Sea Turtle, scientifically known as Lepidochelys olivacea, was intercepted during a routine patrol by Customs officers at about 10.30pm on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The command said the officers sighted a suspicious individual carrying a sack along the border route, but the suspect abandoned the bag and fled into a nearby bush upon noticing the patrol team. According to a statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Customs, John Tunde Ayagbalo, examination of the abandoned sack revealed the live sea turtle concealed inside. He said the animal was immediately secured and kept in safe custody before being handed over to relevant wildlife authorities for proper care, rehabilitation and eventual release into its natural habitat. The Acting Customs Area Controller, Seme Area Command, Deputy Comptroller Norman Olisah Alumanah, described the interception as a demonstration of the vigilance and professionalism of officers in tackling wildlife trafficking. Alumanah warned smugglers, poachers and their collaborators against using the nation’s borders as corridors for illegal wildlife trade, adding that the command had intensified patrols, surveillance and intelligence gathering across its area of responsibility. He also called on residents of border communities to provide credible intelligence to support the fight against wildlife trafficking. The Customs boss said the command would complement enforcement operations with stakeholder education and sensitisation on endangered species, their ecological importance and the legal implications of their unauthorised trade. Wildlife trafficking remains a major environmental crime, threatening biodiversity and the survival of endangered species through illegal exploitation for meat, eggs, shells, traditional medicine and the exotic pet trade. Nigeria is a signatory to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which regulates international trade in endangered wildlife and plant species. The convention is domesticated in Nigeria through the Endangered Species (Control of International Trade and Traffic) Act, Cap E9, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. nigeria.description: By Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has completed the 21-day monitoring of all 62 contacts linked to the imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease (BVD), a form of Ebola disease, confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026, with no secondary infections recorded. The Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this on Friday during a media briefing in Abuja, saying the last contact had been discharged from monitoring after testing negative for the virus. Idris said 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period, but laboratory tests confirmed that none had contracted the disease. “The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case. “A total of 62 contacts were identified, placed in quarantine and followed up by our public health teams. During the monitoring period, 13 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease, and all tested negative,” he said. The index case was a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman, who tested positive for the virus in Abuja on October 20. She was subsequently medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26. Providing an update on her condition, Idris said the woman had recovered and been discharged from a hospital in Geneva. He also disclosed that seven additional suspected cases were reported and investigated in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the past three weeks. All seven cases tested negative for the virus. However, the NCDC chief cautioned against interpreting the completion of contact monitoring as a formal declaration that the outbreak was over. He explained that such a declaration would depend on established public health criteria and findings from continued surveillance. “It is important to note that the completion of contact monitoring does not, by itself, constitute a formal declaration that an outbreak is over. Such a determination must be based on the applicable public health criteria and the findings of ongoing surveillance. “Nigeria therefore remains vigilant, particularly given the continued occurrence of Ebola virus disease in the DRC,” he said. nigeria.title: 2027: Tinubu, Atiku, Obi not there for Nigeria — Sule Lamido
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Jigawa State Governor and PDP chieftain, Sule Lamido, has dismissed President Bola Tinubu, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, as unsuitable options for Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general election. Lamido stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, where he was asked which of the three political figures could attract the Northern vote in the forthcoming presidential election. Giving his assessment, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain said none of the three contenders was in a position to address Nigeria’s challenges. Peter Obi, Tinubu, Atiku — none of them is there for Nigeria.” The former Jigawa governor also declared his support for the PDP’s presidential candidate, Professor Sandy Onor, insisting that he remained committed to the opposition party and would not vote for Tinubu in 2027. Asked whether he had endorsed Tinubu for a second term, Lamido said he remained a PDP member and would vote for his party’s candidate. He said, “I am PDP through and through. I am voting for my candidate, Professor Sandy Onor; that is my candidate. What I’m saying is that we have somebody called Professor Onor on that ballot. I’m voting him.” Lamido’s remarks come amid controversy over claims that he had endorsed Tinubu’s re-election bid after Vice-President Kashim Shettima reportedly listed him among former Jigawa governors backing the President ahead of 2027. However, the Jigawa State chapter of the PDP had earlier dismissed the claim, insisting that Lamido had neither endorsed Tinubu nor defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. entertainment.title: Ayobami Esther Akinnagbe: Organisational Mistakes Start-up Founders Should Avoid
entertainment.description: Two women engaged in a professional meeting, discussing business in a modern office setting. Image by RDNE Stock project for Pexels . There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. sports.title: Couch: 3 quick takes on Michigan State basketball's 106-72 win over Northern Iowa
sports.description: 1. 106 points scored, but some lesson for MSU against Northern Iowa EAST LANSING — With the score 19-2, barely more than five minutes into the game, you had to wonder if Northern Iowa could get to 10. Michigan State’s defense was that relentless. The Panthers looked that overwhelmed. By halftime, Northern Iowa had 44 points. MSU 59. The officials 33 fouls called, playing their part in what might have been a very watchable half, but instead wasn’t. Two minutes into the second half, it was MSU 62, Northern Iowa 51. This as an actual game, with Jasah Jervis’ 3-point shooting primarily responsible for keeping the Panthers at bay. In the end, it was a comfortable 106-72 MSU win over an offensively skilled opponent that had a lot more faith in its ability to shoot and score than it appeared in the opening minutes. There are couple lessons MSU can take from this game: One, that you can’t knock out every lesser foe with an early punch. Some of these teams have some confident dudes who play. If you see a team with two or three guys on the court who look like Howdy Doody, assume they can shoot and are better than they look. They’re out there for a reason. Second, MSU has to learn how to be physical defensively and on the glass without fouling. Because while the Spartans withstood having seven players with two fouls each in the first half Friday, that’ll be a problem against some opponents. The officials were too quick with the whistle Friday. There were a number of fouls called that just weren’t. But there were a lot that were. This was a handsy and physical game, a clumsily physical game in the first half especially. Ultimately, we’re nitpicking a 34-point win over a solid Missouri Valley Conference team where the Spartans scored over 100 points, got 44 points out of their starting backcourt (Jeremy Fears Jr., 24, and Jervis, 20) and took control firmly as the second half went along. But that’s where this team is now. After Tuesday’s wire to wire win over Duke, all that’s left to do against Northern Iowa is nitpick. And this group left Tom Izzo plenty to pick at. 2. Jervis, again, leads record 3-point shooting night It’s becoming clear shooting isn’t going to be a problem for this MSU basketball team. And that it’ll likely be a strength. You can’t take that just from a record-setting night against Northern Iowa, where the Spartans hit a program-record 18 3-pointers (on 37 attempts) against a Northern Iowa team that’s never heard of a close-out defensively. sports.description: A San Jose Earthquakes flag is seen during a MLS match between the San Jose Earthquakes and Houston Dynamo FC on Sept. 12, 2026 at PayPal Park in San Jose. (Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Less than two weeks before the San Jose Earthquakes are scheduled to finally play their very first playoff match at PayPal Park, owner John Fisher is selling the team. On Friday, the Earthquakes announced that Heath Freeman, a media executive best known for being the co-founder and president of hedge fund Alden Global Capital, has agreed to purchase the team and its home stadium from Fisher and his partners. Major League Soccer's board has already approved the ownership change, the team said, and "the transaction is expected to close in the coming weeks." Sportico was first to report about Fisher's sale to Freeman and reported the sale price was $625 million, a figure that an Earthquakes team official confirmed was accurate to SFGATE. Fisher has been looking to sell the Earthquakes since June 2025. At the time, Fisher was in the beginning stages of building the A's ballpark in Las Vegas, and was seeking more finances to build the new stadium. The Las Vegas ballpark 's construction has progressed steadily, but the estimated cost has ballooned from as low as $1.5 billion originally to north of $2 billion . The reviled A's owner purchased the Quakes in 2007, getting a chance to revive the MLS franchise after the first iteration of the club ended when the franchise moved to Houston. Fisher privately financed the building of the stadium now known as PayPal Park, spending $100 million to build the stadium that opened in 2015. Between the A's move to Las Vegas and the pending Earthquakes sale, it seems Fisher will now no longer be a sports owner in the region that his family has called home for his entire life. Freeman is a graduate of Duke who played on the school's football team as a walk-on kicker. An avid sports fan, he's an owner of a Professional Bull Riders team, the executive chairman of the AVP beach volleyball league, and a major booster of his alma mater as well as the University of Miami's volleyball team. Outside of the sports world, Freeman has become a vilified figure in the media world thanks to the moves of Alden. sports.description: EAST LANSING – Tom Izzo wanted to see how Michigan State basketball would respond to success. The Spartans did so in triplicate. Jeremy Fears Jr. and Jasiah Jervis led an outside shooting barrage for No. 5 MSU, which broke a school record with 18 3-pointers en route to a 104-72 victory over Northern Iowa on Friday, Nov. 13, at Breslin Center. ON GUARD: Michigan State's ferocious defense is its 'best brand of basketball' The previous single-game record was 17 3-pointers, set against Purdue on Feb. 20, 2014, and tied against Rutgers on Jan. 31, 2016. Freshman Julius Avent drained the record-breaker with 50 seconds to play as MSU finished 18-for-37 (48.6%) from behind the arc. The Spartans also turned 16 UNI turnovers into 31 points. Greyson Uelmen scored 16 points and three others added 11 apiece for the Panthers (2-2). It was over when ... MSU put the game away swiftly, with a 19-2 opening salvo that included five 3-pointers in six attempts. Fears and Scott had two apiece, and Jervis had another. The Spartans built their lead to 20 on Jervis’ second 3 as part of a 7-for-9 start beyond the arc. By halftime, five different MSU players hit at least one 3-pointer. Scott had three 3s and 11 points with four boards at the break. That sizzling 10-for-16 shot-making from deep led to a 59-44 halftime advantage, the most points the Spartans have scored in a first half since getting 64 in a 104-83 blowout of Green Bay on Dec. 18, 2018. sports.title: UNC handed first loss of the season in sloppy game against Georgia
sports.description: Nov 13, 2026; Chapel Hill, North Carolina, USA; Georgia Bulldogs guard Marcus Millender (4) lays the ball up against North Carolina Tar Heels guard Neo Avdalas (17) and guard Terrence Brown (1) during the first half at Smith Center. Mandatory Credit: Zachary Taft-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Unlike UNC’s game against Wyoming on Tuesday, the Tar Heels turned in a first half they couldn’t fully make up for in their 78-70 loss to Georgia on Friday. Carolina shot just 25% from the field and from three in the first 20 minutes and allowed the Bulldogs to close on a 9-0 run to hold a 38-31 advantage at the break. The loss snapped a 21-game win streak at the Dean Dome for the Heels. The second half was definitely a better offensive effort for UNC. They shot 40% from the field in the second half. Georgia was able to make 14 three-pointers, though, and that was enough to come out on top of a close game. Terrence Brown was very good again, leading the team with 21 points and zero turnovers. Neo Avdalas and Isaiah Denis were the only other Tar Heels in double figures with 14 and 11 points, respectively. Carolina made just nine of their 38 three-point attempts. They were also pushed around on the boards again, losing the battle on the glass 52-43. Carolina led by as many as nine points in the game, and looked in the second half like they may have figured things out similarly to their win earlier in the week. Georgia is not Wyoming, though, and they were not going to go down easily. The Heels’ poor rebounding and lack of offensive efficiency, combined with the Bulldogs’ threes, proved to be enough for Georgia to walk away with a win. It was an immensely frustrating game because it was very easy to see how the outcome could have been different. Allowing Georgia extra possessions often ended with the Bulldogs getting another three. Carolina also seemingly abandoned running actual offense down the stretch to their detriment as the game slipped away. These are not things you can afford to do against real Power 4 competition. UNC will have a week to fix what they can ahead of next Friday’s game against Marshall.

sports.title: Texas expected to arrive in Baton Rouge late Friday after FAA ground stop
sports.description: TOPSHOT - Planes wait on the tarmac at Chicago O'Hare International Airport in Chicago, on November 13, 2026. The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a ground stop at all US airports. (Photo by KAMIL KRZACZYNSKI / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images At 2:48 p.m. Central, the social media team for the No. 6 Texas Longhorns posted a video of players boarding the chartered plane heading to Baton Rouge for Saturday’s matchup against the No. 21 LSU Tigers. Bayou bound🤘 pic.twitter.com/gCkcnOkl2e — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 13, 2026 Minutes after the video was posted, the Federal Aviation Administration issued an extraordinarily rare nationwide ground stop for all US airports due to a “temporary telecommunications outage,” only the second ground stop issued by the FAA since September 11, 2001. “Out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted. Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis,” the FAA posted on Twitter. Unable to depart for Baton Rouge, the Longhorns deplaned and headed back to campus in an attempt to maintain the typical Friday routine of a meal, walk-through, and meetings. Brown posted his story to Twitter at 7:14 p.m. Central; approximately a minute later, the FAA lifted the ground stop and an official announcement was posted about 15 minutes later. “At 8:15 tonight, Eastern time, we’ve opened up the airspace,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a news briefing. “Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It’s going to be slow. Duffy publicly encouraged grounded football teams across the country to reach out directly to the FAA to schedule flight times to allow Saturday’s games to happen as scheduled. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin blamed the outage on upgrades patched onto the FAA’s old systems. WOW MULLIN SAYS THE UPGRADES DUFFY PUT IN CAUSED THE OUTAGE “The new technology was overwhelming the older system” pic.twitter.com/GG6oW7CnVF — Acyn (@Acyn) November 14, 2026 Just before 8 p.m. Central, the Horns remained on the Forty Acres and hopeful to leave Austin on Friday with a subsequent upgrade indicating that Texas is expected to arrive in Baton Rouge before midnight after taking off just after 10 p.m. Central.

technology.title: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed
technology.description: GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That's around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. Among GLP-1 users, nearly half (44 percent) reported using their GLP-1 in a way that was different from how it was prescribed. Users skipped doses, delayed getting refills, and used smaller doses than prescribed, among other changes. More than half of the people modifying how they used the drug said the changes were because of cost or availability reasons. Cost and access barriers were most pronounced among younger GLP-1 users. technology.title: Chinese AI labs are training models on Nvidia's Blackwell despite export controls, says ex-OpenAI engineer
technology.description: US export controls are not stopping AI labs in China from using restricted Nvidia chips, according to a report from a former OpenAI engineer. Will DePue, who left the AI giant earlier this year to launch Unemployment Labs, an AI research consultancy, published forensic evidence showing that "DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group have gained access to Nvidia's Blackwell GPUs, despite restrictions on exporting these chips to China, and are using that hardware to create their AI models." "This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it," said DePue in a social media post . "When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern – a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model." It doesn't sound that insane. The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang followed from revelations that he had an affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who, in 2023, founded Singapore-based Megaspeed International. That company is reportedly under investigation by US authorities for allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips to China. Huang's departure coincides with a renewed push to tighten US chip export controls. House Speaker Mike Johnson supports the idea . And there are at least four bills awaiting consideration that aim to limit China's access to leading edge AI tech: the AI Overwatch Act, the Chip Security Act, Match Act, and the Cloud Security Act. On Monday, US Senators Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) cited Jensen Huang's "relationship with a suspected Chinese spy" as a justification for passing the AI Overwatch Act, which would codify the Trump administration's existing chip export controls. The Trump administration on Thursday said it's not sure whether Alice Huang was a spy, an allegation denied by Beijing and currently under investigation by the FBI. Whatever the case, the current rules clearly are not working. Only a few weeks ago, Lava, an Israel-based security company, said it had found "32 Nvidia B300 GPUs, part of Nvidia's Blackwell Ultra generation, through publicly exposed monitoring endpoints with IP addresses geolocated to China." These GPUs, Lava noted, are subject to US export controls [PDF]. technology.description: Chalk up a new record for vulns. The number of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) found and disclosed so far in 2026 surpassed 100,000 on Friday - more than double 2025’s total - and the reason can be summed up in two letters: AI. “It’s kind of wild,” Josh Bressers, VulnCheck’s director of coordinated vulnerability disclosure, told The Register . “The thing that almost scares the bejesus out of me is while 100K sounds like a lot, in a couple years we're going to say, remember when it was only 100K?” As of the time of our interview, about 4 pm UTC on Friday, VulnCheck counted 100,222 CVEs, he said. Microsoft alone added 1,094 security flaws to the total count on Tuesday, following 1,474 vulnerabilities the month before. “There's no denying the fact that vulnerability hunting with AI is driving a majority of what we're seeing.” All the major CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) - these are the organizations authorized by the CVE program to assign unique identifiers to security vulnerabilities - like VulnCheck, Microsoft, Oracle, GitHub, and other large enterprise IT vendors “are just screaming into the atmosphere right now,” Bressers said. “It’s AI.” Meanwhile, the percentage of these bugs that are exploited in the wild remains relatively consistent. About 1.4 percent (1,363) of the CVEs published this year have been added to VulnCheck’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. “But obviously, as the number of CVEs grows, [1 percent] of 1,000 is a lot different than [1 percent] of 100,000,” Bressers said. Plus, as other security researchers have documented, the window between the public release of a security patch and attackers developing working exploits – often by reverse engineering the patch while end users are still applying the fix – is rapidly shrinking. The security firm said China-linked groups such as Vault Panda and Genesis Panda moved even faster, launching attacks within 24 hours of disclosure. LogicLens and Receipts claim to identify logical fallacies , flag reports that misrepresent information, detect content that attempts to polarize an issue, and the like. It also cites sources, so if, for example, you need to call someone out on their BS, you’ll have ammunition. Or, if you’re trying to fact-check something before sharing it, you can get a more accurate view of the situation, and maybe post something else instead. Using the Chrome extension is as simple as clicking on its icon in the list of extensions in the browser. On iOS, the Receipts app is found as a share option. technology.title: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits
technology.description: Elephants live in some of the most complex and resilient societies in the animal kingdom. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together. Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time. Anastasia Madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka. They found that, once losses began to outpace newcomers, the elephants’ society didn’t just get smaller. It fractured. Accidental savanna Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka was created in the 1970s around a reservoir on one of the country's four major rivers. “Before that, it was basically a tropical deciduous forest,” said Shermin de Silva, an ecologist at UC San Diego and senior author of the study (de Silva started the Udawalawe Elephant Research Project in 2006). The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972. science.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
science.description: null This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed. In more recent years, most notably 1999 , 2001 and 2002 , lesser Leonid displays of up to "only" a few thousand meteors per hour took place. Unfortunately, that's not likely to be the case this year. In fact, comparatively speaking, this is going to be a lean year for the Leonids chiefly because of the expected lack of any significant activity. Although the Leonids are one of the most famous of all the annual meteor displays, this year they're not likely to be very productive. It's probable they are going to be rather weak and there probably will be long stretches when not a single Leonid will be seen. I'll explain why in a moment. First, let's find out about this shower's lineage. What causes the Leonids? The Leonids are so named because the shower's radiant point, from where the meteors seem to fan out, is located within the constellation of Leo the Lion, from the backward question mark pattern of stars known as " The Sickle." The meteors are caused by the Tempel-Tuttle comet , which sweeps through the inner solar system every 33⅓ years. Each time the comet passes closest to the sun it leaves a "river of rubble" in its wake: a dense trail of dusty debris. A meteor storm becomes possible if the Earth were to score a direct hit on a fresh dust trail ejected by the comet over the past several centuries. The "lion's share" (no pun intended) of comet dust can be found just ahead and trailing behind Tempel-Tuttle. That comet last swept through the inner solar system in 1998. That's why spectacular meteor showers were seen in 1999, 2001 and 2002, with declining numbers thereafter. science.title: Rocket Lab launching 100th space mission early on Nov. 14: Watch it live
science.description: null Rocket Lab will launch its 100th space mission early Saturday morning (Nov. 14), and you can watch the milestone liftoff live. An Electron rocket topped with a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite is scheduled to launch from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site on Saturday, during a window that opens at 12:30 a.m. EST (0530 GMT; 6:30 p.m. local time). The mission, which Rocket Lab calls "The Mountain God Rises," will be the 100th to date for the California-based company. You can watch it live via Rocket Lab, or directly via the company . Coverage will begin about 30 minutes before launch. The Electron rocket that will fly Rocket Lab's 100th mission sports some special livery. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) Rocket Lab launched for the first time in May 2017, sending the brand-new Electron up on a test flight from New Zealand. That effort failed, but Electron bounced back on its second-ever liftoff, delivering several cubesats to low Earth orbit (LEO) in January 2018. In the years since, the 59-foot-tall (18 meters) Electron has become one of the most prolific and reliable rockets in the world, carrying small payloads to the final frontier for a variety of customers. And it's hitting the century mark in record-breaking fashion: No commercially developed rocket has gotten there faster, not even SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9 , according to Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck. "It's an unprecedented milestone for a commercial small-lift orbital rocket, and a threshold rarely crossed in modern spaceflight," Beck said on Monday (Nov. 9), during Rocket Lab's third-quarter earnings call with investors. "But what matters most to us and our customers is that we have achieved a 96% reliability rate across 99 launches." Electron will meet the moment in style on Saturday morning, thanks to some fancy livery. "Black rocket 🤝 Golden milestone. Electron is all dressed up for launch 100," Rocket Lab said via X on Tuesday (Nov. 10), in a post that shared a photo of the specially painted first stage. Not all of Rocket Lab's missions have gone orbital, it should be noted: A suborbital variant of Electron known as HASTE , which customers use to test technologies in a hypersonic flight environment, has nine missions under its belt to date. The patch for Rocket Lab's "The Mountain God Rises" mission, which will be the company's 100th launch to date. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) "The Mountain God Rises" will be Rocket Lab's 11th launch to date for the Tokyo-based company iQPS, which is building a constellation of three dozen synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites in LEO. If all goes to plan, Electron's upper "kick stage" will deploy a single iQPS spacecraft 357 miles (575 kilometers) above Earth. science.title: Think you have good eyesight? Try counting the stars in the Pleiades tonight
science.description: null Every autumn, I conduct an eyesight test that no reputable optometrist would understand. I go outside, find the Pleiades and count how many stars I can see. Usually I start confidently. One, two, three, four, five. Then things become contentious. Is that another star? Did I actually see it, or did I decide I ought to see it because I know it's there? I look away, look back and begin again. This is not, I should emphasize, a meaningful test of eye health. What it tests, rather, is how badly I've prepared for looking at the night sky. The Pleiades sit roughly 444 light-years away in Taurus and are right now becoming extremely convenient in the evening sky. You don't need a telescope to find them. You don't even need binoculars. In fact, you're likely to catch their collective brightness in your peripheral vision every time you go outside and look up. But every November the Pleiades remind me that naked-eye observing isn't as simple as opening the back door and looking up. How many Pleiades I can see can change depending on what I do during the next 10 minutes. What's happening and when to look You can easily see the Pleiades as a bright misty patch in your peripheral vision during winter. (Image credit: Haitong Yu via Getty Images) The Pleiades, also known as Messier 45 (M45) or the "Seven Sisters," are an open star cluster in Taurus. They're one of the closest clusters to the solar system and some of the youngest stars you can see with the naked eye — just 100 million years old. They're basically newborns. In mid-November, they rise in the east in the early evening and climb higher as the night progresses, making this an excellent time to get acquainted with them. Look east after dark for a tiny, compact group of stars. If you know Orion, which rises later, the Pleiades are above and to the right of it from mid-northern latitudes. Nearby you'll also find orange Aldebaran and the much broader V-shaped Hyades cluster. The Hyades are closer to the sun , but their stars are about 625 million years old. The name "Seven Sisters" creates an immediate observational trap: people assume they're supposed to see seven stars. That's not necessarily true. In fact, six is a common naked-eye result under decently dark conditions (note that the shape of the six brightest is like a mini Big Dipper /Plough), while people with sharp eyesight under darker skies may see more. The cluster itself contains about 1,000 stars. The number you personally distinguish depends on eyesight, sky brightness, atmospheric conditions and how well your eyes have adapted to darkness. That makes M45 much more interesting to me than a simple tick-box target. So tonight, don't just find the Pleiades — count them. And yes, it does look an awful lot like " The Martian ," doesn't it? There's a lot of survival gameplay on display here that mirrors Mark Watney's tale of survival on the Red Planet, as your stranded protagonist is forced to explore the Martian surface to acquire resources, grow plants, and repair their base. That comparison to Andy Weir's sci-fi masterpiece does fall away as you get further into the trailer, though, when the horror part of the game's description comes into play: Flickering lights, creepy figures stalking the halls of your Martian habitat, and blood dripping from the walls. There's no release date scheduled at this time, with the 'Martian Isolation' Steam page simply listing it as "coming soon," though the YouTube trailer description does say it "will be available on Steam in 2027". You can't pre-order yet, but if this looks like your jam, you can add it to your wishlist. Beyond that, we know shockingly little about this title. It's the debut game from Golden Milestone Studio, but there's very little information out there beyond a name. The latest blog post on the game's Steam page says that they're a "small team," but what we've seen so far is encouraging. There seems to be a pronounced split between the survival and horror elements of the game along the day/night cycle. Daytime sees you exploring the Martian surface, smashing rocks, cleaning solar panels, and doing sick jumps on a quad bike. I'm always looking for new ways to shatter my psyche and possibly soil my pants, so I'll be keeping a close eye on this one. In the meantime, I do need to get back and finish " Routine ."
